scr_cash_card_maintenance_list.purpose: Lists every petty cash (PC) debit card issued across properties — cardholder, property, status (active, on hold, cancelled), limit and current balance — as the control register for the card program.
scr_cash_card_maintenance_list.outcome: Treasury can see at a glance which cards are live, who holds them and how much each can spend.
scr_cash_card_maintenance_list.rootCause: Each active card is a standing spending authority at a site. When staff turn over at leasing offices, cards must be reassigned, held or cancelled; the register is where that is controlled.
scr_cash_card_maintenance_list.ifSkipped: Cards stay active with departed employees and continue to be spent without anyone reviewing them.
gaap: COSO 2013 — safeguarding assets and access termination
redFlags: Active cards assigned to terminated employees

scr_cash_issuing_pc_cards_in_bulk_via_im.purpose: Issues many petty cash cards at once from an import template — typically when rolling the program out across a portfolio or onboarding a newly managed group of properties.
scr_cash_issuing_pc_cards_in_bulk_via_im.outcome: Cards for dozens of properties are issued consistently with correct limits and holders in one step.
scr_cash_issuing_pc_cards_in_bulk_via_im.rootCause: Portfolio roll-outs and take-overs require cards for many sites at once. Manual issuance invites inconsistent limits and holder errors.
scr_cash_issuing_pc_cards_in_bulk_via_im.ifSkipped: Roll-outs are slow and limits vary arbitrarily between sites.
redFlags: Imported limits above the petty cash policy

scr_cash_viewing_open_transactions_on_a_.purpose: Shows a card's transactions that have not yet been submitted as expenses — purchases awaiting coding, receipts or approval.
scr_cash_viewing_open_transactions_on_a_.outcome: Treasury and managers see spending that has happened but not been accounted for.
scr_cash_viewing_open_transactions_on_a_.rootCause: Card purchases hit the balance immediately but are recorded as expenses only when submitted. Open transactions are unaccounted spending and a leading indicator of misuse.
scr_cash_viewing_open_transactions_on_a_.ifSkipped: Spending goes unrecorded and unreviewed, and month-end expenses are understated.
redFlags: Open transactions older than 30 days

scr_cash_deleting_an_unissued_pc_card.purpose: Deletes a petty cash card record that was created but never issued to a cardholder — for example set up for the wrong property.
scr_cash_deleting_an_unissued_pc_card.outcome: Unused card records are removed so the register reflects only real cards.
scr_cash_deleting_an_unissued_pc_card.rootCause: Unissued card records clutter the register and could be activated and issued later without the proper request and approval.
scr_cash_deleting_an_unissued_pc_card.ifSkipped: The register contains phantom cards that confuse reviews.
redFlags: Deleting cards that had funding loaded

scr_cash_replacing_a_lost_or_stolen_pc_c.purpose: Cancels a lost or stolen petty cash card and issues a replacement, moving the remaining balance to the new card.
scr_cash_replacing_a_lost_or_stolen_pc_c.outcome: Exposure on the lost card stops immediately while the site keeps its purchasing ability.
scr_cash_replacing_a_lost_or_stolen_pc_c.rootCause: A lost card can be used by whoever finds it until it is cancelled. Replacement must be fast and must carry over the balance so funds are not lost.
scr_cash_replacing_a_lost_or_stolen_pc_c.ifSkipped: Fraudulent charges accumulate on the lost card, and the site is left without a card.
redFlags: Charges on the lost card after the reported loss date

scr_cash_issue_card_page_card_maintenanc.purpose: The card detail page opened from card maintenance, showing holder, property, limits, status and authorized users for an existing card.
scr_cash_issue_card_page_card_maintenanc.outcome: All attributes of one card available for review or change.
scr_cash_issue_card_page_card_maintenanc.rootCause: Card changes (limits, users, status) must be made on the specific card record with a trail of who changed what.
scr_cash_issue_card_page_card_maintenanc.ifSkipped: Card changes are made without a clear record.
redFlags: Card changes without an approver

scr_cash_adding_or_removing_authorized_u.purpose: Adds or removes staff authorized to use a property's petty cash card — for example when a leasing agent leaves or a new maintenance supervisor starts.
scr_cash_adding_or_removing_authorized_u.outcome: Only current, authorized staff can use the card.
scr_cash_adding_or_removing_authorized_u.rootCause: Site staff turnover is high in multifamily. Authorized-user lists that are not updated leave former employees able to spend.
scr_cash_adding_or_removing_authorized_u.ifSkipped: Former employees keep access to card funds.
redFlags: Authorized users not updated after terminations

scr_cash_increasing_or_decreasing_the_ca.purpose: Changes a petty cash card's spending limit — raising it for a busy season (pool opening supplies) or lowering it after misuse.
scr_cash_increasing_or_decreasing_the_ca.outcome: Card limits match the site's legitimate needs and risk.
scr_cash_increasing_or_decreasing_the_ca.rootCause: Limits cap potential loss. They must be adjustable but controlled, since raising limits increases exposure.
scr_cash_increasing_or_decreasing_the_ca.ifSkipped: Limits are either too low for legitimate needs (pushing staff to personal cards) or too high for the risk.
redFlags: Limit increases approved by the cardholder's own manager only, without treasury

scr_cash_adding_funds_to_a_pc_card.purpose: Loads additional funds onto a petty cash card, for users with the Change Funds permission, typically after submitted expenses are approved.
scr_cash_adding_funds_to_a_pc_card.outcome: The card is replenished for continued site purchases, with funding recorded from the property's operating account.
scr_cash_adding_funds_to_a_pc_card.rootCause: Replenishment is the key control point: funds should be added only after prior spending is submitted and approved, like an imprest petty cash fund.
scr_cash_adding_funds_to_a_pc_card.ifSkipped: Cards run dry and staff use personal funds; if done without review, unaccounted spending is refunded blindly.
redFlags: Funds added while open transactions are unsubmitted

scr_cash_putting_a_pc_card_on_hold.purpose: Temporarily freezes a petty cash card — during an investigation, extended staff leave or while receipts are overdue.
scr_cash_putting_a_pc_card_on_hold.outcome: Spending stops immediately without cancelling the card.
scr_cash_putting_a_pc_card_on_hold.rootCause: Holds give managers leverage to get receipts submitted and a way to stop spending while suspicious activity is reviewed.
scr_cash_putting_a_pc_card_on_hold.ifSkipped: Spending continues during investigations or while accountability is lacking.
redFlags: Cards on hold for months without resolution

scr_cash_canceling_or_inactivating_a_pc_.purpose: Permanently cancels or inactivates a petty cash card when a site no longer needs it, the holder leaves, or the property is sold.
scr_cash_canceling_or_inactivating_a_pc_.outcome: The card can no longer be used, and any remaining balance is returned to the property.
scr_cash_canceling_or_inactivating_a_pc_.rootCause: Cards for sold properties or departed staff are standing exposure; cancellation removes it and recovers the unspent balance.
scr_cash_canceling_or_inactivating_a_pc_.ifSkipped: Cards remain usable after they should be closed.
redFlags: Remaining balances not recovered on cancelled cards

scr_cash_card_transactions_page.purpose: Shows all transactions for a petty cash card, where cardholders code them, attach receipts and submit them as expenses.
scr_cash_card_transactions_page.outcome: Card purchases become coded, receipted expenses ready for approval.
scr_cash_card_transactions_page.rootCause: Card spending needs the same coding and support as any other expense. This page is where the cardholder turns raw card activity into accounted expenses.
scr_cash_card_transactions_page.ifSkipped: Card spending is never coded or supported.
redFlags: Transactions submitted without receipts

scr_cash_submitting_an_expense_for_a_pc_.purpose: Submits a coded card transaction, with receipt, as an expense for approval and posting.
scr_cash_submitting_an_expense_for_a_pc_.outcome: The expense is recorded to the right property and GL account once approved.
scr_cash_submitting_an_expense_for_a_pc_.rootCause: Submission moves spending from 'money gone' to 'expense recorded and approved', which is necessary before replenishment.
scr_cash_submitting_an_expense_for_a_pc_.ifSkipped: Expenses are not recorded and replenishment cannot be approved.
redFlags: Personal-type merchants submitted as business expenses

scr_cash_splitting_a_pc_card_transaction.purpose: Splits one card transaction across multiple GL accounts — for example a hardware store purchase that includes both maintenance supplies and office supplies.
scr_cash_splitting_a_pc_card_transaction.outcome: Mixed purchases are coded accurately to each expense category.
scr_cash_splitting_a_pc_card_transaction.rootCause: Single receipts often cover different expense types; coding everything to one account distorts budget variances.
scr_cash_splitting_a_pc_card_transaction.ifSkipped: Budget lines are misstated by mixed purchases.
redFlags: Splits that do not sum to the transaction total

scr_cash_card_transactions_list.purpose: Lists petty cash card transactions across all cards and properties, with status (open, submitted, approved, excluded), for oversight.
scr_cash_card_transactions_list.outcome: Treasury and regional managers can review card spending portfolio-wide.
scr_cash_card_transactions_list.rootCause: Oversight across all cards is needed to spot patterns (split purchases to avoid limits, unusual merchants) that are not visible card by card.
scr_cash_card_transactions_list.ifSkipped: Misuse patterns across cards go unnoticed.
redFlags: Repeated transactions just under the card limit

scr_cash_excluding_a_pc_card_transaction.purpose: Excludes a card transaction from expense processing — for example a card load or a merchant refund that should not be treated as an expense.
scr_cash_excluding_a_pc_card_transaction.outcome: Non-expense card activity does not flow into the P&L.
scr_cash_excluding_a_pc_card_transaction.rootCause: Card activity includes loads and refunds that are not expenses. Excluding them keeps expense reporting accurate, but excluding real purchases would hide spending.
scr_cash_excluding_a_pc_card_transaction.ifSkipped: Loads and refunds are treated as expenses; misuse hides real purchases.
redFlags: Purchases excluded rather than submitted

scr_cash_re_including_an_excluded_pc_car.purpose: Restores a petty cash card transaction that was excluded from expense processing by mistake, so the cardholder can code it, attach the receipt and submit it.
scr_cash_re_including_an_excluded_pc_car.outcome: Real purchases wrongly excluded are brought back into the expense and approval flow.
scr_cash_re_including_an_excluded_pc_car.rootCause: Excluded transactions never become expenses and are never reviewed. A real purchase excluded in error is unrecorded spending — the same outcome as misuse — so it must be restorable.
scr_cash_re_including_an_excluded_pc_car.ifSkipped: Real spending stays off the books, expenses are understated and nobody reviews the purchase.
redFlags: Frequent exclude/re-include cycles on the same card

scr_cash_open_subledger.purpose: Re-opens a closed Cash Management period so cash transactions (deposits, transfers, bank fees) can again be posted to it — for example to record a bank fee discovered late.
scr_cash_open_subledger.outcome: A controlled window to correct cash activity in a closed period.
scr_cash_open_subledger.rootCause: Occasionally a material cash transaction must be recorded in the period it occurred. Reopening is possible but changes reported cash, so it must be deliberate.
scr_cash_open_subledger.ifSkipped: Material corrections are forced into the wrong period; if reopening is uncontrolled, reported cash changes after the fact.
redFlags: Cash periods reopened after bank recs were approved

scr_cash_opening_a_period.purpose: Procedure to open a Cash Management period — both for opening the next period and for reopening a closed one.
scr_cash_opening_a_period.outcome: The period is available for cash postings.
scr_cash_opening_a_period.rootCause: Periods must be opened before activity can post; reopening closed ones must follow the same controlled steps.
scr_cash_opening_a_period.ifSkipped: Cash transactions cannot post or are forced into other periods.
redFlags: Multiple periods left open at once

scr_cash_close_subledger.purpose: Closes a Cash Management period independently of other subledgers, preventing further deposits, transfers and bank entries from posting into it.
scr_cash_close_subledger.outcome: Reconciled cash periods are locked so recs stay valid.
scr_cash_close_subledger.rootCause: Once a bank rec is approved, any new posting in that period breaks it. Closing the cash subledger protects approved reconciliations.
scr_cash_close_subledger.ifSkipped: Late cash postings break approved bank recs and next month's beginning balance.
redFlags: Cash subledger left open after recs approved

scr_cash_closing_a_period.purpose: Procedure to close a Cash Management period after bank reconciliations are complete.
scr_cash_closing_a_period.outcome: The cash period is locked in line with the close calendar.
scr_cash_closing_a_period.rootCause: Closing in sequence — after recs are approved and before the GL is closed — keeps cash stable for owner reporting.
scr_cash_closing_a_period.ifSkipped: Cash remains open to backdated postings.
redFlags: Cash closed before all recs finalized

scr_cash_print_payment_copies_results_pa.purpose: Shows the results of a payment-copies search — the checks and electronic payments matching the chosen filters — ready to print or email.
scr_cash_print_payment_copies_results_pa.outcome: A selected set of payment copies for vendors, auditors or files.
scr_cash_print_payment_copies_results_pa.rootCause: Vendors often ask for proof of payment, and auditors sample disbursements. Copies are produced from the results list.
scr_cash_print_payment_copies_results_pa.ifSkipped: Proof of payment requests take longer to answer.
redFlags: Results including voided payments sent as proof of payment

scr_cash_emailing_and_printing_copies_of.purpose: Emails or prints copies of issued vendor checks — front image and remittance detail — to answer vendor payment inquiries or to file as disbursement evidence.
scr_cash_emailing_and_printing_copies_of.outcome: Vendors receive proof of payment and the file holds disbursement support.
scr_cash_emailing_and_printing_copies_of.rootCause: Vendors frequently claim non-receipt or misapply payments. Sending a copy of the check resolves the inquiry and prevents the vendor from re-billing, which would risk a duplicate payment.
scr_cash_emailing_and_printing_copies_of.ifSkipped: Vendors keep chasing payment, re-bill the same invoice, and duplicate payments become more likely.
redFlags: Check copies emailed to addresses not on the vendor record

scr_cash_reconcile_bank_account_page_2.purpose: The matching workspace of the new bank reconciliation tool (Bank - New!), where imported bank transactions are matched to G/L cash transactions with intelligent matching and a running difference.
scr_cash_reconcile_bank_account_page_2.outcome: Bank and book activity are matched with far less manual effort than in the legacy tool.
scr_cash_reconcile_bank_account_page_2.rootCause: The new tool is designed around imported bank data and rule-based matching, so preparers spend their time on exceptions rather than routine matches — important for offshore teams handling many accounts.
scr_cash_reconcile_bank_account_page_2.ifSkipped: Preparers stay on slower manual matching and miss close deadlines.
redFlags: Large numbers of manual overrides of suggested matches

scr_cash_filtering_and_sorting_transacti.purpose: Filters and sorts transactions in the new reconciliation tool's matching page to isolate unmatched items by amount, type or date.
scr_cash_filtering_and_sorting_transacti.outcome: Exceptions are found quickly among high-volume activity.
scr_cash_filtering_and_sorting_transacti.rootCause: Even with auto-matching, residual exceptions must be isolated from thousands of matched lines.
scr_cash_filtering_and_sorting_transacti.ifSkipped: Exceptions are overlooked in large accounts.
redFlags: Filters left on that hide unmatched items at finalization

scr_cash_reconciling_an_account_manually.purpose: Manual matching in the new tool for items auto-matching missed — many-to-one deposits, split transfers, or keying differences.
scr_cash_reconciling_an_account_manually.outcome: Remaining exceptions are matched with preparer judgment.
scr_cash_reconciling_an_account_manually.rootCause: Some bank-book relationships (one bank credit for several book deposits) cannot be resolved by rules and need a person.
scr_cash_reconciling_an_account_manually.ifSkipped: Legitimate items carried as false reconciling items.
redFlags: Manual matches with amount differences

scr_cash_reconciling_accounts_with_intel.purpose: Configures reconciliation rules (Setup > Reconciliation Rules) that automatically match bank and G/L transactions — by amount and date tolerance, check number, reference or description patterns.
scr_cash_reconciling_accounts_with_intel.outcome: Most routine matches happen automatically, consistently across all accounts.
scr_cash_reconciling_accounts_with_intel.rootCause: Rules encode the matching logic an experienced accountant applies, so offshore teams can scale across many accounts without losing accuracy.
scr_cash_reconciling_accounts_with_intel.ifSkipped: Matching remains manual and inconsistent across preparers.
redFlags: Rules with wide date or amount tolerances that create wrong matches

scr_cash_matching_bank_transactions_with.purpose: Matches bank transactions to each other without a G/L transaction — for example a bank debit and its same-day reversal by the bank.
scr_cash_matching_bank_transactions_with.outcome: Bank-side pairs that net to zero are cleared without book entries.
scr_cash_matching_bank_transactions_with.rootCause: Banks sometimes post and reverse items (errors, returned deposits re-presented). These pairs should cancel on the bank side alone.
scr_cash_matching_bank_transactions_with.ifSkipped: Offsetting bank pairs remain unmatched and clutter the rec.
redFlags: Bank-only matches that do not net to zero

scr_cash_matching_different_transaction_.purpose: In the new tool, matches a group of different transaction types whose net is zero — for example a book deposit and its reversal — clearing them together.
scr_cash_matching_different_transaction_.outcome: Offsetting book entries that never reached the bank are cleared.
scr_cash_matching_different_transaction_.rootCause: Reversals and voids in the same period create book-only pairs that must be cleared together or they sit as outstanding items forever.
scr_cash_matching_different_transaction_.ifSkipped: Permanent outstanding items that obscure real ones.
redFlags: Zero-net matches of unrelated items

scr_cash_matching_a_range_of_checks_quic.purpose: Quick Match in the new tool clears a range of check numbers at once when all cleared at their issued amounts.
scr_cash_matching_a_range_of_checks_quic.rootCause: High check volume makes one-by-one matching impractical; range matching is efficient but must not mask altered amounts.
scr_cash_matching_a_range_of_checks_quic.ifSkipped: Slow check clearing; misuse hides altered checks.
redFlags: Quick match used where bank amounts differ from issued amounts

scr_cash_unmatching_a_transaction_2.purpose: Undoes an incorrect match in the new (Bank - New!) reconciliation tool — typically an auto-match that paired two same-amount items that do not belong together — so both return to the unmatched lists.
scr_cash_unmatching_a_transaction_2.outcome: Wrong matches are corrected before finalizing, keeping real exceptions visible.
scr_cash_unmatching_a_transaction_2.rootCause: Rule-based matching on amount can pair the wrong items when many transactions share amounts (identical rent payments). A wrong match hides a real unmatched item.
scr_cash_unmatching_a_transaction_2.ifSkipped: A wrong match hides a genuine exception, such as an unrecorded bank debit, until it surfaces months later.
redFlags: Frequent unmatching indicating poorly tuned matching rules

scr_cash_exporting_bank_reconciliation_t.purpose: Exports matched and unmatched transactions from the new tool to Excel for analysis and review.
scr_cash_exporting_bank_reconciliation_t.outcome: Portable reconciliation detail for reviewers and follow-up.
scr_cash_exporting_bank_reconciliation_t.rootCause: Reviewers and site teams need reconciliation detail outside the system to investigate aged items.
scr_cash_exporting_bank_reconciliation_t.ifSkipped: Follow-up on reconciling items is slower.
redFlags: Exports altered before being shared
